_meta.indication: SOVALDI is a hepatitis C virus (HCV) nucleotide analog NS5B polymerase inhibitor indicated for the treatment of chronic hepatitis C (CHC) infection as a component of a combination antiviral treatment regimen.

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, single-arm trial of 12 weeks of SOVALDI + peginterferon alfa 2a + ribavirin compared to a pre-specified historical control
pivotal_trials.population: Treatment-naïve subjects with genotype 1, 4, 5 or 6 chronic HCV infection
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Sustained virologic response at 12 weeks post-treatment (SVR12)

nct_ctgov.title: Sofosbuvir With Peginterferon Alfa 2a and Ribavirin for 12 Weeks in Treatment-Naive Subjects With Chronic Genotype 1, 4, 5, or 6 HCV Infection

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, open-label, active-controlled trial of 12 weeks SOVALDI + ribavirin vs 24 weeks peginterferon alfa 2a + ribavirin
pivotal_trials.population: Treatment-naive subjects with genotype 2 and 3 HCV
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Sustained virologic response at 12 weeks post-treatment (SVR12)
pivotal_trials.result: Overall SVR 67% (171/256) with SOVALDI+RBV vs 67% (162/243) with Peg-IFN alfa+RBV; treatment difference 0.3% (95% CI: -7.5% to 8.0%)

nct_ctgov.title: Phase 3 Study of Sofosbuvir and Ribavirin

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial of 12 weeks SOVALDI + ribavirin (N=207) vs placebo (N=71)
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects who are interferon intolerant, ineligible or unwilling (genotype 2 or 3 HCV)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Sustained virologic response at 12 weeks post-treatment (SVR12)
pivotal_trials.result: Overall SVR 78% (161/207) with SOVALDI+RBV vs 0/71 with placebo (p < 0.001)

nct_ctgov.title: Sofosbuvir + Ribavirin for 12 Weeks in Subjects With Chronic Genotype 2 or 3 Hepatitis C Infection Who Are Interferon Intolerant, Interferon Ineligible or Unwilling to Take Interferon

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blinded trial of 12 or 16 weeks of SOVALDI + ribavirin in prior interferon-based treatment failures
pivotal_trials.population: Previously treated genotype 2 or 3 subjects who did not achieve SVR with prior interferon-based treatment (relapsers and nonresponders)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Sustained virologic response at 12 weeks post-treatment (SVR12)
pivotal_trials.result: Overall SVR 50% (51/103) with 12 weeks vs 71% (70/98) with 16 weeks SOVALDI+RBV

nct_ctgov.title: Sofosbuvir + Ribavirin for 12 or 16 Weeks in Treatment Experienced Subjects With Chronic Genotype 2 or 3 HCV Infection (FUSION)

key_safety: The most common adverse events (≥20%) with SOVALDI + ribavirin were fatigue and headache; with SOVALDI + peginterferon alfa + ribavirin were fatigue, headache, nausea, insomnia and anemia. In the SOVALDI+Peg-IFN+RBV 12-week arm fatigue 59%, headache 36%, nausea 34%, insomnia 25%, anemia 21%.
target_moa: Sofosbuvir is a nucleotide prodrug that is metabolized intracellularly to the active uridine analog triphosphate GS-461203, which is incorporated into HCV RNA by the NS5B RNA-dependent RNA polymerase and acts as a chain terminator, inhibiting viral replication.

advisory_committee.vote: The Antiviral Drugs Advisory Committee convened October 25, 2013 and voted unanimously to support approval of sofosbuvir.

description.text: Expanded sofosbuvir plus ribavirin to pediatric patients 12-17 years or ≥35 kg with chronic HCV genotype 2 or 3 without cirrhosis or with compensated cirrhosis

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application proposes to expand the patient population for sofosbuvir in combination with ribavirin to include the treatment of pediatric patients 12 to 17 years of age or weighing at least 35 kg with chronic hepatitis C virus genotype 2 or 3 infection without cirrhosis or with compensated cirrhosis based upon the data from Trial GS-US-334-1112.

description.text: Expanded to include pediatric patients 3 years and older weighing at least 17 kg with genotype 2 or 3 chronic HCV, in combination with ribavirin

citations.quote: - The use of SOVALDI® (sofosbuvir) 200 mg tablets for the treatment of chronic hepatitis C virus, genotype 2 or 3 infection in pediatric patients, 3 years of age and older, weighing at least 17 kg, without cirrhosis or with compensated cirrhosis for use in combination with ribavirin.

basis.text: Breakthrough therapy designation was granted for sofosbuvir on October 10, 2013 under IND 106739.

citations.quote: Breakthrough therapy designation was granted for sofosbuvir on October 10, 2013 under the IND 106739.

basis.text: The original NDA was submitted April 6, 2013 and reviewed under priority review.

citations.quote: The original NDA Application was submitted on April 06, 2013 and is currently under priority review.

summary.text: Sofosbuvir was the first-in-class HCV NS5B inhibitor submitted in the U.S.; the NDA was submitted April 6, 2013 under priority review, granted breakthrough therapy designation on October 10, 2013, reviewed with an Antiviral Drugs Advisory Committee that unanimously supported approval, and approved as a standard (non-accelerated) approval.

citations.quote: Sofosbuvir is the first-drug-in class submitted for marketing application in the United States. The original NDA Application was submitted on April 06, 2013 and is currently under priority review. Breakthrough therapy designation was granted for sofosbuvir on October 10, 2013 under the IND 106739.

The application was presented before the Antiviral Drugs Advisory Committee on October 25, 2013. The Committee voted unanimously to approve SOF for the treatment of GT1, GT2, GT3 and GT4 CHC as a component of a combination treatment regimen in adults with compensated liver disease including cirrhosis as well as for a subpopulation of the pretransplant population with HCC meeting Milan criteria.

requirement.text: 2110-1: Conduct a trial to evaluate the PK, safety and treatment response (SVR) of SOVALDI as a component of an antiviral regimen in pediatric subjects 3 through 17 years of age with chronic hepatitis C.

citations.quote: 2110-1 Conduct a trial to evaluate the pharmacokinetics, safety and treatment response (using sustained virologic response) of SOVALDI (sofosbuvir) as a component of an antiviral treatment regimen in pediatric subjects 3 through 17 years of age with chronic hepatitis C.

requirement.text: 2110-2: Collect and analyze long-term safety data (≥3 years follow-up) for subjects enrolled in the pediatric trial, including growth, sexual maturation, and resistance characterization.

citations.quote: 2110-2 Collect and analyze long-term safety data for subjects enrolled in the pediatric SOVALDI (sofosbuvir) pharmacokinetic, safety and efficacy trial described in 2110-1. Data collected should include at least 3 years of follow-up in order to characterize the long-term safety of sofosbuvir in pediatric subjects, including growth assessment, sexual maturation and characterization of sofosbuvir resistance-associated substitutions in viral isolates from subjects failing therapy.
